name: compare
description: A choice told as the choice, the criteria, each option against the criteria, and the verdict with when the other option wins, for tool and design decisions.
ending: The viewer can make the choice with the criteria, and the next action is to score their own case on the same table.

name: history-lesson
description: A history told as then, turning points, what went wrong, the fix, and what it means now, for topics with a lesson for today.
ending: The viewer takes one lesson from the past, and the next action is to look for the same risk in their own work.

name: how-it-works
description: A mechanism told as the question, the parts, one flow through the parts, and the limits, for technology and science topics.
ending: The viewer can trace the flow without help, and the next action is to see the same flow in a real tool or log.

name: incident-review
description: An incident told as what happened, the timeline, the cause, what changed, and the lesson, for blameless reviews of outages.
ending: The viewer knows the cause and the change that stops a repeat, and the next action is to check their own system for the same weak point.

name: problem-fix
description: A PR told as problem, change, effect, and risk, for code reviews and release notes.
ending: The viewer knows what the PR fixes and what to watch, and the next action is to review the diff.

name: system-tour
description: A repo told as purpose, main parts, one request through it, and how to start, for onboarding to a codebase.
ending: The viewer knows where each main part lives, and the next action is to run the start command.
